mainTopic: Rain in its season, the stories of חוני המעגל, and the start of the story of his grandson אבא חלקיה
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא explaining that rain 'in its season' means rain on Tuesday nights and Friday nights. It proves this with two stories. In the days of שמעון בן שטח, crops grew huge. In the days of הורדוס, rain fell only at night while the בית המקדש was being built. The גמרא then tells the full story of חוני המעגל from the משנה. He drew a circle and swore not to leave it until it rained, and after a drizzle and then a flood, proper rain came. Since one may not pray against too much good, he ended the rain with a thanksgiving offering and a prayer for relief. שמעון בן שטח criticized his boldness but compared him to a beloved son, and the סנהדרין praised him with פסוקים from איוב. רבי יוחנן then tells how חוני slept seventy years and woke to find no one believed him, and רבא concludes: either friendship or death. Finally, the story of his grandson אבא חלקיה begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What 'in their season' means
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that rain 'in its season' means rain on Tuesday nights and Friday nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In their season' means on the nights before Wednesday and on the nights before שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a ברייתא that explains words from a פסוק about rain. Here it explains the word בעתם, 'in their season.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal rain is not only rain in the right month but rain on the right nights. These are nights when people are usually not out, so the rain bothers no one. The next two steps bring stories that show this kind of rain really happened.

keyTerms.meaning: In their season, at the right time

steps.confusionAlert: לילי רביעיות does not mean Wednesday night. A Jewish day starts the evening before, so it means Tuesday night, which is the start of Wednesday. The same goes for שבת: Friday night.

phrases.english: "In their season" means
phrases.notes: This is explaining a word from ויקרא 26:4, 'I will give your rains in their season.'

phrases.english: on the nights before Wednesday and on the nights before Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא from before this section that explains a פסוק about rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain 'in its season' means rain that falls on Tuesday nights and Friday nights.

steps.title: The amazing crops in the days of שמעון בן שטח
steps.stepSummary: In the days of שמעון בן שטח, rain fell on exactly those nights and the crops grew huge. Samples were saved to show later generations what sin takes away.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know this because in the days of שמעון בן שטח, rain fell on Tuesday nights and Friday nights, and the crops grew enormous: wheat as big as kidneys, barley as big as olive pits, and lentils as big as gold coins. People saved some of them as a sample for future generations, to show how much sin costs us, as the פסוק says: 'Your sins have turned these things away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its explanation with a real time in history when rain fell on exactly those nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows how great the blessing can be when rain comes at the right time. The saved samples teach a lesson: our crops are smaller now because of sin, not because the land cannot do better. The פסוק from ירמיהו backs up that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A great Sage of the Second Temple period
They tied up, wrapped and saved

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the blessing of rain into a moral lesson: what we are missing is a result of our actions.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בִּימֵי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
phrases.english: For so we found in the days of Shimon ben Shetach
that rain fell for them
on the nights before Wednesday and on the nights before Shabbat,
until the wheat grew as big as kidneys,
and the barley as big as olive pits,
and the lentils as big as gold coins,
and they tied up some of them as a sample for future generations,
to show how much damage sin causes,
as it is said: "Your iniquities have turned away these things,
and your sins have held back the good from you."

steps.triggerLanguage: שכן מצינו בימי שמעון בן שטח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a historical example to support the explanation in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That 'in their season' means rain on Tuesday nights and Friday nights, and that such rain is a great blessing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical memory of the days of שמעון בן שטח, together with ירמיהו 5:25.

steps.title: Night-only rain while הורדוס built the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: While הורדוס was building the בית המקדש, rain fell only at night, so the work never stopped. The people understood that Heaven was helping them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also found that in the days of הורדוס, when they were building the בית המקדש, rain fell at night. In the morning the wind blew, the clouds scattered, the sun shone, and the people went out to work. They knew they were doing Heaven's work.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second example of rain that came at a perfect time and harmed no one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story adds that rain timing can show that Heaven approves of what people are doing. The rain never got in the way of building the בית המקדש, so the builders saw it as a sign that this was Heaven's work.

keyTerms.meaning: King הורדוס, who rebuilt the Second בית המקדש
The building of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Rain 'in its season' is rain that comes when it helps and does not disturb: on nights when people are not out, or only at night while important work is being done.

phrases.english: And we likewise found in the days of Herod,
when they were busy building the Temple,
that rain would fall at night,
and the next day the wind would blow,
the clouds would scatter, and the sun would shine,
and the people would go out to their work,
and they knew that the work of Heaven was in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second historical example, parallel to step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That perfectly timed rain is a real kind of blessing and a sign of Heaven's favor.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical memory of rain during the building of the בית המקדש under הורדוס.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about חוני המעגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the opening words of its story about חוני המעגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'There was a story in which they sent a message to חוני המעגל, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the words of the משנה. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא tells the full story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the story briefly. The גמרא quotes its opening words so we know which part of the משנה it is now explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an event that happened
חוני the circle-drawer, a famous צדיק known for his prayers for rain
And so on; the quote continues

phrases.english: There was an incident in which they sent a message to Choni HaMe'agel, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא about rain in its season and returns to a new part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens the discussion of the משנה's story of חוני המעגל.

steps.title: No rain in אדר, and חוני's first prayer fails
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells the story: most of אדר passed with no rain. The people asked חוני to pray, he prayed, and still no rain fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Once, most of אדר went by and it still had not rained. They sent a message to חוני המעגל: 'Pray, and rain will fall!' He prayed, but no rain fell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the משנה's story in more detail. It begins with a serious drought late in the winter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reaching the end of אדר with no rain means the whole winter's rain has failed, so the situation is serious. The people trust that חוני's prayer will work. His first plain prayer does not bring rain, which sets up the more dramatic step that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
Most of the month of אדר
Pray! (as a request), or 'he prayed' (as a report)

steps.confusionAlert: The same word הִתְפַּלֵּל appears twice. The first time the people are telling חוני 'Pray!' The second time it reports what happened: 'He prayed.'

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Once, most of Adar had passed
and no rain had fallen.
They sent a message to Choni HaMe'agel:
Pray, and rain will fall!
He prayed, but no rain fell.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן פעם אחת יצא רוב אדר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the full story behind the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a late-winter drought the people asked חוני to pray, and his first prayer was not answered.

steps.title: חוני draws a circle like חבקוק
steps.stepSummary: חוני drew a circle, stood inside it, and followed the example of חבקוק the prophet, using a פסוק as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: He drew a circle and stood inside it, the way חבקוק the prophet did, as the פסוק says: 'I will stand on my watch and take my place on the tower.'
steps.whatsHappening: After his first prayer fails, חוני does something dramatic: he draws a circle and stands inside it. The ברייתא shows he had a source for this in חבקוק the prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains his nickname, המעגל, 'the circle-drawer.' The ברייתא reads the פסוק about standing 'on the tower' as describing a closed place חבקוק made for himself. חוני copied that, so his act has a basis in a prophet's actions. The next steps continue the story.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows where חוני got his name and that his unusual act copied a prophet. This prepares the rest of his famous story.

phrases.english: He drew a circle and stood inside it,
the way Habakkuk the prophet did,
as it is said: "Upon my watch I will stand
and set myself upon the tower, and so on."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after his first prayer fails, חוני takes a stronger step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני drew a circle and stood inside it, following the example of חבקוק based on חבקוק 2:1.

steps.title: חוני swears not to move until it rains
steps.stepSummary: חוני tells ה׳ that the people depend on him, and he swears not to leave his circle until ה׳ has mercy. A light drizzle begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: חוני said: Master of the world, Your children are looking to me because I am close to You, like a member of Your household. I swear by Your great Name that I will not move from here until You have mercy on them. Then rain started to drip.
steps.whatsHappening: Standing inside the circle from the last step, חוני makes a bold oath before ה׳. The first small answer comes: a few drops of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The circle from step 6 now has a meaning: חוני has trapped himself inside it with an oath. He bases his request on being like a 'member of the household' of ה׳, someone who can ask boldly. The rain that comes is only a trickle, which sets up the students' complaint.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the world, a way of calling out to ה׳
Like a member of the household, someone close and familiar

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the world!
Your children have turned their faces to me,
because I am like a member of Your household.
I swear by Your great Name
that I will not move from here
until You have mercy on Your children.
Rain began to drip.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! בָּנֶיךָ שָׂמוּ פְּנֵיהֶם עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after drawing the circle, חוני now prays and swears inside it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני swears not to leave the circle until rain comes, and a light drizzle begins.

steps.title: The students say the drizzle is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The students complain that these few drops seem to fall only so that חוני's oath is technically fulfilled, not to save anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said: רבי, we are counting on you so that we will not die. It seems to us this rain is falling only to release you from your oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The students react to the drizzle and push חוני to ask for more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their point is sharp: a few drops 'count' as rain, so חוני's oath is kept, but the people still face starvation. This sets up חוני's next, more specific request.

keyTerms.meaning: We look to you, so that we will not die

phrases.english: His students said to him: Rabbi!
We look to you, and may we not die,
it seems to us

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין גְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִין אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר שְׁבוּעָתְךָ.
phrases.english: that the rain is falling only to release your oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי! רְאִינוּךְ וְלֹא נָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the drizzle from step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students say the drizzle only fulfills the oath and does not save the people.

steps.title: חוני asks for more, and the rain becomes violent
steps.stepSummary: חוני asks for rain that will fill pits, ditches and caves. The rain then falls furiously, with huge drops.
steps.simpleTranslation: חוני said: This is not what I asked for. I asked for rain that fills pits, ditches and caves. Then the rain came down in fury, each drop as big as the mouth of a barrel. The Sages estimated that no drop was smaller than a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני makes his request more exact, and the rain swings to the other extreme.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני's new request is about amount: enough water to fill the storage pits for the year. The answer is too much and too violent. This is the second of three kinds of rain in the story.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not what I asked for
Pits, ditches and caves, places where water was stored

phrases.english: He said: This is not what I asked for,
but rain for pits, ditches and caves.
It fell furiously,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁכׇּל טִפָּה וְטִפָּה כִּמְלֹא פִּי חָבִית.
phrases.english: until every single drop was as big as the mouth of a barrel.
And the Sages estimated
that no drop was less than a log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַלְתִּי, אֶלָּא גִּשְׁמֵי בּוֹרוֹת שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: חוני answers the students' complaint by asking ה׳ for more rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני asks for enough rain to fill the storage places, and it comes down violently.

steps.title: The students say the rain will destroy the world
steps.stepSummary: The students now complain the other way: this rain looks like it is coming to destroy the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said: רבי, we are counting on you so that we will not die. It seems to us this rain is falling only to destroy the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The students repeat their opening words, but now their worry is the opposite one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as step 8 on purpose. Only the ending changes, from 'to release your oath' to 'to destroy the world.' This pushes חוני to make a third, more careful request.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Rabbi,
we look to you, and may we not die,
it seems to us

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין גְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִין אֶלָּא לְאַבֵּד הָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: that the rain is falling only to destroy the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, רְאִינוּךְ וְלֹא נָמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the violent rain from step 9, using the same words as step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students say the violent rain threatens to destroy the world.

steps.title: Rain of blessing falls, until the people ask for it to stop
steps.stepSummary: חוני asks for rain of goodwill and blessing. It falls normally but keeps going, so the people climb to הר הבית and ask him to pray for it to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: חוני said before ה׳: This is not what I asked for. I asked for rain of goodwill, blessing and generosity. Then the rain fell properly, until all the people went up to הר הבית because of the rain. They said to him: רבי, just as you prayed for it to fall, pray for it to go away.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני's third request is answered with normal, good rain. But it does not stop, and the people ask him to pray again. This sets up חוני's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the rain is right in kind, but it keeps falling until the people need higher ground. Their request is natural: if prayer brought the rain, prayer should end it. חוני's answer will show that this is not so simple.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain of goodwill, blessing and generosity

phrases.english: He said before Him: This is not what I asked for,
but rain of goodwill, blessing and generosity.
It fell in its proper way,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁעָלוּ כׇּל הָעָם לְהַר הַבַּיִת, מִפְּנֵי הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: until all the people went up to the Temple Mount because of the rain.
They said to him: Rabbi,
just as you prayed that it should fall,
so pray that it should go away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַלְתִּי, אֶלָּא גִּשְׁמֵי רָצוֹן בְּרָכָה וּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: חוני responds to the students' fear of destruction with a third request. The people then raise a new request.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper rain falls, but so much that the people ask חוני to pray for it to stop.

steps.title: חוני's tradition: no praying against too much good
steps.stepSummary: חוני answers that he has a tradition that one does not pray over an excess of good.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I have a tradition that we do not pray about too much good.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני answers the people's request from the last step with a rule he received from his teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain, even too much of it, is still blessing. So חוני holds that one should not pray for good to be taken away. This is the rule the משנה itself points to, and it explains why ending the rain needs a different approach.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition
An excess of good, too much good

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main rule behind the story: we do not pray to remove too much blessing. The next step shows how חוני still finds a proper way to ask.

phrases.english: He said to them: This is my tradition,
that one does not pray over an excess of good.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כָּךְ מְקוּבְּלַנִי שֶׁאֵין מִתְפַּלְּלִין עַל רוֹב הַטּוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the people's request at the end of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One does not pray to stop an excess of good, so חוני will not simply pray for the rain to end.

steps.title: חוני brings a thanksgiving bull and prays for relief
steps.stepSummary: Even so, חוני asks for a thanksgiving bull. Leaning his hands on it, he tells ה׳ that Israel cannot handle too much punishment or too much good, and asks that the rain stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, bring me a bull for a thanksgiving offering. They brought it, and he leaned both hands on it and said: Master of the world, Your people Israel whom You took out of Egypt cannot handle too much good or too much punishment. When You were angry, they could not stand it. When You poured good on them, they could not stand it. May it be Your will that the rain stop and there be relief in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Despite his tradition, חוני finds a way to ask. He combines thanks for the rain with a prayer for relief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני does not ask ה׳ to take the blessing back. He first thanks ה׳ with the bull, then explains that the people are too weak to hold so much good. He asks for relief, not for an end to blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull brought as a thanksgiving offering
He leaned both his hands on it

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, הָבִיאוּ לִי פַּר הוֹדָאָה.
phrases.english: Even so, bring me a bull for a thanksgiving offering.
They brought him a thanksgiving bull,
he leaned his two hands on it,
and said before Him: Master of the world!
Your people Israel, whom You took out of Egypt,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לֹא בְּרוֹב טוֹבָה וְלֹא בְּרוֹב פּוּרְעָנוּת.
phrases.english: cannot bear either too much good or too much punishment.
You were angry with them, and they could not stand it,

phrases.aramaic: הִשְׁפַּעְתָּ עֲלֵיהֶם טוֹבָה — אֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד,
phrases.english: You poured good upon them, and they could not stand it.
May it be Your will that the rain stop,
and that there be relief in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן, הָבִיאוּ לִי פַּר הוֹדָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after stating the rule in step 12, חוני finds a fitting way to ask for the rain to end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני brings a thanksgiving offering and prays for relief, not for the blessing to be removed.

steps.title: The rain stops at once and the sun comes out
steps.stepSummary: Right away the wind blows, the clouds scatter, the sun shines, and the people go out to gather truffles and mushrooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately the wind blew, the clouds scattered, the sun shone, and the people went out to the field and brought back truffles and mushrooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows that חוני's last prayer is answered at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ending proves that a prayer framed as thanks plus a request for relief is accepted. The people even gain from the heavy rain: truffles and mushrooms grew in the soaked fields.
steps.whatToRemember: חוני's rain came in three stages: a drizzle, a violent flood, then proper blessed rain. Since one may not pray against too much good, he ended it with a thanksgiving offering and a prayer for relief, and it worked at once.

phrases.english: Immediately the wind blew, and the clouds scattered,
and the sun shone,
and the people went out to the field
and brought themselves truffles and mushrooms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the immediate result of חוני's prayer in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rain stops right away, and the people benefit from the growth it brought.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח says חוני deserved נידוי
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח tells חוני he would have put him in נידוי. If this had been a time like אליהו's, when rain was locked by אליהו's oath, חוני's oath would have caused a חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמעון בן שטח sent a message to חוני: If you were not חוני, I would put you in נידוי. Imagine these were years like the years of אליהו, when the keys of rain were in אליהו's hand. Wouldn't the name of Heaven have been disgraced through you?
steps.whatsHappening: The story's aftermath begins: the great leader שמעון בן שטח criticizes how חוני prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני swore he would not leave his circle until it rained. If אליהו had sworn at the same time that it would not rain, one of the two oaths would have turned out false. That kind of clash is a חילול השם, so חוני's behavior was risky.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the חכמים in חוני's generation
Ban or excommunication, a formal penalty from the חכמים
The keys of rain, meaning control over the rain

phrases.english: Shimon ben Shetach sent to him:
If you were not Choni,
I would decree a ban on you.
For if the years were like the years of Eliyahu,
when the keys of rain were in Eliyahu's hand,
phrases.notes: אליהו swore it would not rain (מלכים א 17:1). חוני swore he would not leave his circle until it did, so both oaths could not come true.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְצָא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְחַלֵּל עַל יָדְךָ,
phrases.english: wouldn't the name of Heaven be found desecrated through you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the miracle ends, a leading חכם reacts critically to חוני's conduct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's oath could have caused a חילול השם, so he deserved נידוי.

steps.title: חוני is like a beloved son pampered by his father
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח explains why he cannot punish חוני‎: ה׳ treats him like a father who gives a pleading son everything he asks for.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what can I do to you? You plead with ה׳ and He does what you want. You are like a son who pleads with his father and gets his way. The son says: Abba, take me to bathe in hot water. Wash me with cold water. Give me nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates. And the father gives him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח turns around and explains why, despite everything, he will not punish חוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with חוני's behavior is real, but ה׳ clearly loves him and answers him every time. The son in the משל keeps changing his requests (hot water, then cold), just as חוני asked for rain, then a different rain, then for it to stop. The father still says yes each time.

keyTerms.meaning: Pleads or coaxes like a pampered child

steps.confusionAlert: This is not praise for being demanding. שמעון בן שטח still disapproves; he is only saying he can't punish someone ה׳ treats with such love.

phrases.english: But what can I do to you,
since you plead before God
and He does your will for you,
like a son who pleads with his father
and he does his will for him,
and he says to him: Father,
take me to bathe me in hot water.
Rinse me with cold water.
Give me nuts, almonds,
peaches and pomegranates —
and he gives him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the threatened נידוי from step 15 will not actually be imposed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's special closeness to ה׳ prevents שמעון בן שטח from punishing him.

steps.title: A פסוק describes חוני's parents rejoicing
steps.stepSummary: שמעון בן שטח ends by applying a פסוק from משלי to חוני: his father and mother will be glad.
steps.simpleTranslation: About you the פסוק says: Your father and mother will be glad, and she who bore you will rejoice.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון בן שטח closes his message by connecting חוני to a פסוק about a child who makes his parents proud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though he was critical, שמעון בן שטח ends on praise. חוני's closeness to ה׳ is something that brings joy, like a son who delights his parents.

keyTerms.meaning: She who gave birth to you

phrases.english: And about you the verse says:
"Your father and your mother will be glad,
and she who bore you will rejoice."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Caps the father-son משל with a supporting פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני is like a child who makes his parents happy.

steps.title: The סנהדרין sends חוני a פסוק of praise
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that the חכמים of לשכת הגזית sent חוני a פסוק from איוב praising him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: What did the members of לשכת הגזית send to חוני המעגל? "You will decree a matter and it will be fulfilled for you, and light will shine on your ways."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a second reaction to חוני, this time from the סנהדרין. It is fully positive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike שמעון בן שטח's mixed message, the great court praises חוני outright. The פסוק they send is explained phrase by phrase in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught, introducing a ברייתא
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the סנהדרין sat

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
What did the members of the Chamber of Hewn Stone send
to Choni the Circle-Drawer?
"You will decree a matter and it will be established for you,
and light will shine upon your ways."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה שָׁלְחוּ בְּנֵי לִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, fully positive reaction to חוני alongside שמעון בן שטח's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סנהדרין praised חוני with a פסוק from איוב.

steps.title: Explaining the סנהדרין's פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains both halves of the פסוק: חוני decrees below and ה׳ fulfills it above, and his prayer lit up a dark generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You will decree a matter": you decreed from below, and ה׳ fulfills your word from above. "Light will shine upon your ways": a generation that was dark, you lit up with your prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now explains what each part of the פסוק means for חוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half matches חוני's oath and demands: his words on earth were carried out in Heaven. The second half refers to the drought. A generation suffering in 'darkness' was saved and lit up because of his תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: חוני gets two reactions. שמעון בן שטח criticizes his boldness but accepts that ה׳ loves him like a son. The סנהדרין praises him fully: his decree was fulfilled in Heaven and his prayer saved a dark generation.

phrases.english: "You will decree a matter" —
you decreed from below,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַיֵּים מַאֲמָרְךָ מִלְמַעְלָה.
phrases.english: and the Holy One, Blessed be He, fulfills your word from above.
"And light will shine upon your ways" —
a generation that was dark
you lit up with your prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains phrase by phrase the פסוק quoted in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ fulfills חוני's decrees, and his prayer saved his generation.

steps.title: The rest of the פסוק from איוב praises חוני for saving an unworthy generation
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא keeps reading the פסוקים in איוב phrase by phrase. Each phrase is about a generation that was low, sinful, or not innocent, and חוני's prayer saved it anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'When they were brought low, you said: Rise up.' A generation that was low, you raised it up with your prayer. 'He saves the one with lowered eyes.' A generation bowed down by its sin, you saved it with your prayer. 'He will rescue the one who is not innocent.' A generation that was not innocent, you rescued it with your prayer. 'He will be rescued by the cleanness of your hands.' You rescued it through the clean work of your hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its explanation of the praise that the חכמים of לשכת הגזית sent to חוני, one phrase of the פסוק at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 read the first phrases as 'you decree and ה׳ fulfills' and 'you lit up a dark generation.' The new phrases add that the generation did not deserve rain because it was low, sinful, and not innocent. It was saved only through חוני's prayer and his clean deeds.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים praised חוני because his prayer saved a generation that did not deserve to be saved. This ends the first story about חוני on this daf.

phrases.english: "When they were brought low, you said: Rise up"
a generation that was low
you raised it up with your prayer.
"And He saves the one with lowered eyes"
a generation that was bowed down by its sin
you saved it with your prayer.
"He will rescue the one who is not innocent"
phrases.notes: איוב 22:30. The word אִי here means 'not.'

phrases.english: a generation that was not innocent
you rescued it with your prayer.
"And he will be rescued by the cleanness of your hands"
you rescued it through the clean work of your hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא's phrase-by-phrase reading of the פסוקים from איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each phrase of the פסוק is read as praise: חוני's prayer and clean deeds saved a low, sinful, unworthy generation.

steps.title: חוני is puzzled all his life by the פסוק 'we were like dreamers'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that חוני was troubled all his life by the פסוק in תהלים that compares the return to ציון to a dream. He asked how anyone could sleep and dream for seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: All his life, that righteous man was troubled by this פסוק: 'A song of Ascents: When ה׳ brought back the returnees of ציון, we were like dreamers.' He said: Is there anyone who sleeps and dreams for seventy years?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about חוני, told by רבי יוחנן. It sets up the question that the story will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the seventy years of exile to a dream. חוני could not understand this, because no one dreams for seventy years. The story that follows will show that it can happen.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the days of that righteous man,
phrases.notes: 'That righteous man' is חוני, from the story we just finished.

phrases.english: he was troubled over this verse:
"A song of Ascents:
When ה׳ brought back the returnees of Zion,
we were like dreamers"
He said: Is there anyone
who sleeps seventy years in a dream?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about the same person, חוני, after the first story ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני wondered how the seventy-year exile could be compared to a dream, since no one sleeps seventy years.

steps.title: חוני meets a man planting a carob tree for his grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: On the road, חוני sees a man planting a carob tree, which takes seventy years to give fruit. When חוני asks whether he expects to live that long, the man answers that he plants for his descendants, just as his ancestors planted for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day he was walking on the road. He saw a man planting a carob tree. He asked him: After how many years will this tree give fruit? The man said: After seventy years. חוני asked: Are you sure you will live seventy years? The man said: I found a world that already had carob trees. Just as my fathers planted for me, I am planting for my children.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. חוני has a conversation that brings up the number seventy again and prepares for his long sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carob tree takes seventy years to give fruit, the same length as the exile and as the sleep in חוני's question. The man's answer shows that people plant for future generations. That idea will matter when חוני wakes up and sees the planter's grandson.

phrases.english: One day he was walking along the road,
he saw a certain man
who was planting a carob tree.
He said to him: This tree,
after how many years does it bear fruit?
He said to him: Not until seventy years.
He said to him: Is it obvious to you
that you will live seventy years?
He said to him:
I found the world with carob trees in it.
Just as my ancestors planted for me,
I too am planting for my children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story that answers חוני's question about sleeping seventy years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A carob tree takes seventy years to give fruit, and people plant it for their descendants, as their ancestors planted for them.

steps.title: חוני falls asleep, is hidden by rock, and sleeps seventy years
steps.stepSummary: חוני sits down to eat and falls asleep. A rock formation closes around him and hides him, and he sleeps for seventy years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat down and ate bread. Sleep came over him and he slept. A rock formation closed around him and hid him from sight, and he slept for seventy years.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches the event at its center. חוני himself sleeps the seventy years that he thought were impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני had asked how anyone could sleep seventy years. Now it happens to him. The rock hiding him explains why no one found or woke him in all that time.

phrases.english: He sat down and was eating bread,
sleep came over him, and he slept.
A rock formation closed around him,
he was hidden from sight,
and he slept for seventy years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the conversation with the planter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני sleeps hidden for seventy years, the very thing he had questioned.

steps.title: חוני wakes and sees signs that seventy years have passed
steps.stepSummary: When חוני wakes, a man is picking carobs from the tree. The man says he is the planter's grandson, so חוני realizes he slept seventy years. His donkey had also given birth to herd after herd.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he got up, he saw a man gathering carobs from the tree. He asked him: Are you the one who planted it? The man said: I am his grandson. חוני said: I learn from this that I slept seventy years. He saw that his donkey had given birth to herd after herd.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני wakes up and works out from what he sees that he really slept seventy years. This answers his lifelong question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree giving fruit and the planter's grandson picking it show that seventy years have passed. The many generations of donkeys are a second sign. Now חוני knows from his own life that a seventy-year 'dream' is possible.

phrases.english: When he got up,
he saw a certain man
who was gathering from them.
He said to him: Are you the one who planted it?
He said to him: I am his son's son.
He said to him: Learn from this
that I slept for seventy years.
He saw his female donkey,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letters in square brackets, which make it 'his female donkey.'

phrases.english: that had given birth to herd after herd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story, showing what חוני found when he woke up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the planter's grandson and the herds of donkeys, חוני concludes that he slept seventy years.

steps.title: חוני returns home and his family does not believe him
steps.stepSummary: חוני goes home and asks about his son. He learns that only his grandson is alive. When he says who he is, nobody believes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went home and asked: Is the son of חוני המעגל alive? They told him: His son is gone, but his grandson is alive. He said: I am חוני המעגל. They did not believe him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going right after חוני wakes up. He goes home, and his own household does not believe he is חוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His question about his son shows he now understands how much time has passed. The answer that only a grandson is left confirms the seventy years. His family hears his claim to be חוני and refuses to believe him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is he alive? (literally, does he still exist?)

phrases.english: He went to his house and said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people now living in his house.

phrases.english: Is the son of Choni the circle-maker alive?
They said to him: His son is no longer here,
but his son's son is here.
He said to them: I am Choni the circle-maker.
They did not believe him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after חוני realizes he slept for seventy years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוני's own family does not believe that he is חוני.

steps.title: The חכמים praise חוני but do not believe it is him
steps.stepSummary: In the בית המדרש, חוני hears the חכמים say that the learning is as clear as it was in חוני's days. When he tells them he is חוני, they do not believe him or honor him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to the בית המדרש and heard the חכמים saying: Our learning is as clear as in the years of חוני המעגל, because when he came into the בית המדרש he would answer every difficulty the חכמים had. He said to them: I am he. They did not believe him and did not give him the honor he deserved.
steps.whatsHappening: חוני goes to the בית המדרש. The חכמים there praise his old greatness, yet they will not believe that the man in front of them is חוני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sad irony is sharp: the חכמים admire חוני, but only as someone from the past. They do not accept the real חוני standing in front of them. The problem is not only that they doubt him; they also fail to give him proper honor.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or hard question in learning

phrases.english: He went to the study hall,
and heard the Sages saying:
Our teachings are as clear as in the years of Choni the circle-maker,
for when he would come into the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קוּשְׁיָא דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן הֲוָה מְפָרֵק לְהוּ.
phrases.english: he would resolve every difficulty the Sages had.
He said to them: I am he,
but they did not believe him,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא עָבְדִי לֵיהּ יְקָרָא כִּדְמִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and did not give him the honor that was proper for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his family rejects him, the חכמים in the בית המדרש reject him too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים praise חוני's past greatness but do not believe or honor the חוני standing before them.

steps.title: חוני dies of loneliness, and רבא's saying
steps.stepSummary: חוני is heartbroken, prays for mercy, and dies. רבא says this is what people mean by 'either friendship or death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He became very upset, prayed for mercy, and died. רבא said: This is what people mean when they say: Either friendship or death.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of חוני ends with his death. רבא then ties it to a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוני's prayer here is a request to die, because a life with no one who knows or values him is no life for him. רבא draws the lesson that a person needs companionship. Without a חברותא, one is almost better off dead.

keyTerms.meaning: He became upset, deeply hurt (literally, his mind became weak)
As people say (introduces a folk saying)

steps.whatToRemember: חוני's story ends with רבא's lesson: או חברותא או מיתותא. Being cut off from people who know and value you is like death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is one of the classic sources for how much a חברותא matters, both in learning and in life.

phrases.english: He became very upset,
prayed for mercy, and died.
phrases.notes: His prayer was a request to die.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is what people say:
Either friendship or death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of חוני being rejected by everyone, and gives רבא's lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: Either friendship or death. A person without companionship is better off dead.

steps.title: Introducing אבא חלקיה, חוני's grandson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story. אבא חלקיה was חוני's grandson, and when rain was needed the חכמים would send to him to pray, and the rain would come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חלקיה was the grandson of חוני המעגל. When the world needed rain, the חכמים would send to him, he would pray for mercy, and rain would come.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts here. The גמרא introduces אבא חלקיה and tells us his prayers for rain were answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like his grandfather חוני, אבא חלקיה's prayers for rain worked. This sets the background for the specific story the גמרא is about to tell.

keyTerms.meaning: The world, here meaning the people

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חִלְקִיָּה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Abba Chilkiya was the son of Choni the circle-maker's son,
and when the world needed rain,
the Sages would send to him,
and he would pray for mercy, and rain would come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא חִלְקִיָּה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּחוֹנִי הַמְעַגֵּל הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חוני's story to a new story about his grandson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא חלקיה, חוני's grandson, was known for prayers that brought rain.

steps.title: Two חכמים find אבא חלקיה hoeing in the field
steps.stepSummary: During a drought, the חכמים send two חכמים to ask אבא חלקיה to pray. They do not find him at home, so they go out and find him working in a field, and they greet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the world needed rain. The חכמים sent a pair of חכמים to him to ask him to pray for rain. They went to his house and did not find him. They went to the field and found him hoeing, and they greeted him.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets the scene for the rest of the story. The two חכמים find אבא חלקיה working as a simple laborer in a field and greet him. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story now moves from a general description to one specific time. A man whose prayers bring rain is found doing ordinary work, hoeing in a field. The greeting sets up what happens next.

keyTerms.meaning: They greeted him (literally, gave him peace)

phrases.english: One time the world needed rain,
and the Sages sent a pair of Sages to him
to ask him to pray for mercy so that rain would come.
They went to his house and did not find him,
they went to the field
and found him hoeing,
and they greeted him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general description of אבא חלקיה to one specific story about him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two חכמים find אבא חלקיה hoeing in a field and greet him. This sets up the rest of the story.
